rationale:
ROUND 3 on correlation c48b7612. Round 2 returned REVISE — with compliance and render_guardian flipping to APPROVE, so round 1's fixes held. Round 2 found TWO more real defects, both now fixed, and raised one objection that is NOT a council matter and has been routed rather than re-argued.

=== THE TWO REAL DEFECTS ROUND 2 FOUND ===

A. guidelines (edit 7, medium) — MY item_key WAS COARSER THAN MY FINDING, which is this estate's own measured trap almost verbatim: 'a keyed work item whose KEY is coarser than its FINDING drops every finding after the first — the second, DIFFERENT finding hits ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and is gone, and the open row goes on describing the first thing it ever saw' (measured elsewhere at four of five open items naming the WRONG facts, with nothing ever erroring). My key was 'brief-negation:<site_id>' while the finding is a LIST of phrases, and a brief is edited by config at any moment — the exact shape. FIXED: the key now carries a sha256 digest of the sorted phrase set, so correcting one phrase and leaving another files a NEW item describing what is actually there, and close-out retires the stale one with a reason distinguishing 'now clean' from 'the phrases CHANGED'. Both landmines stay satisfied — no finding is dropped, and no open row is rewritten daily (which would bump updated_at and make it unreapable for ever, bugs_closed/213). PROVEN IN PRODUCTION on the live fleet after the fix shipped (v1.0.1322): all 12 site-keyed items closed and 9 refiled under phrase-set keys, in one run.

B. llm_reliability (edit 5, HIGH) — MY SECOND TRUNCATION ARM COULD NOT FIRE. 'output_tokens >= the max_tokens sent' with output_tokens defaulting to 0 when a provider reports no usage is FALSE, so the arm silently never ran — indistinguishable from 'the answer was complete'. FIXED: the three states are now distinct (known-and-at-the-ceiling, known-and-below, UNKNOWN), and UNKNOWN is logged rather than assumed safe. Stated plainly: the load-bearing protection was never that arm — it is the typed aiservice.IsTruncated error, plus the fact that a cut JSON object does not parse and an unparseable answer splices nothing.

=== THE OBJECTION THAT IS NOT A COUNCIL MATTER, AND WHAT WAS DONE WITH IT ===

guardian (edit 4, HIGH) and architecture (edit 4, medium) both said the annotation is default-ON at the registry entries of two of the most-invoked actions in the platform, fleet-wide, arriving inside a single-agent bug fix — and that RFC_022's narrow exception does not cover a default-ON change. BOTH ARE CORRECT AS STATEMENTS OF FACT and I am not arguing with either. Per the owner ruling of 2026-07-28, a scope objection is not answered by resubmitting with better measurements: it is recorded where the change lives and routed to architecture review on its own merits. Filed as architecture_review/RFC_044_default_on_annotation_on_two_shared_render_actions.md, quoting both seats verbatim, with four costed options and an explicit statement that this lane is NOT deciding it. The recommendation there is (a) leave it as an unconsumed observational key or (b) declare an ActionInputSpec on both actions so the optional-key budget can SEE it — explicitly not (c) opt-in default-OFF, because an unwired counter is the exact failure this whole bug is an instance of (copy-editor: live since 2026-08-17, dispatched by nothing).

=== ANSWERED WITH EVIDENCE, NOT CHANGED ===

1. reuse_agent (edit 2, HIGH) — 'section_text.go / unified_extractor.go already walk content_data'. CHECKED, and they solve a different problem. section_text.go exports NormaliseSectionText(rawJSON) string, SectionIdentityKey and SectionTokenSet: it flattens a section to ONE string for identity and dedup, with no field paths and no way to write a value back. unified_extractor.go extracts a NAMED field from collected data. The repair needs (path, text, setter) per prose field so a rewrite lands in the very map the renderer reads — neither can supply that, and building on either would have meant a scan/splice mismatch.
2. reuse_agent (edit 7, medium) — 'why not the discovery_checks framework instead of a CronJob?' Because a discovery check is enabled per discovery agent by a `checks` array, i.e. per site — which reintroduces exactly the property this design refuses everywhere else (the existing voice_tells check is opted into by 9 of 43 sites, which is why it never saw this fault). The question is also fleet-shaped: one global read of the WRITER'S config decides what counts as the brief, and the report is a fleet table. Same reasoning verifier-remit-check records for the same choice.
3. bug_historian (edit 2, medium) — 'no test proves Set() writes through to the SAME map'. There is one: TestSetWritesThrough mutates via the walker and asserts on the ORIGINAL map, including a list-item path. It was in the code and not in the edit list; it is named in the sketch now.
4. bug_historian (edit 5, medium) — 'does it fail closed if the verbatim text has moved by splice time?' Yes, explicitly: the splice is strings.Replace(text, sentence, to, 1) and `if updated == text` is a rejection with reason 'splice_missed'. Named in the sketch now.
5. prior_art_librarian (edit 7, HIGH) — 'a tool listed as operation:add cannot already have a versioned production run'. It can when they happen in one session: written, committed, built (v1.0.1321), deployed and run today, then corrected and rebuilt (v1.0.1322) after this round's item_key finding. The item_type brief_supplies_negation did not exist before this work — its first rows were written by that first run, hours ago.
6. prior_art_librarian (edit 5, medium) — 'the real symbol is ScanBannedClaims, not checkBannedClaims/loadEvidenceBase'. Both exist under those names: checkBannedClaims at validate_page_content.go:1060 and loadEvidenceBase at :1144, and checkBannedClaims itself calls datahelpers.ScanAllBannedClaimsWithSuppressed — so the fleet arm and the negation-suppression behaviour ARE shared, which is what the objection asked to establish.
7. debug_historian (edit 7, medium) — 'how is the un-hold verified against the running pod?' Migration 509's header names it as precondition (1), with the command: read the binary's own build provenance per service, then git merge-base --is-ancestor. Precondition (2) is the per-page budget canary.
8. improvement_guardian (edit 7, medium) — churn protection. Answered by (A): a stable brief produces a stable key and therefore no new row, while a CHANGED brief produces a new row rather than a silently stale one.
9. tooling_provenance (edits 5/6, low) — no queryable decision trail for the agent. DONE: a doc_notes row (subject_type 'decision', subject_key 'page-content-writer') recording why the step exists and the three mechanisms it deliberately is not.
10. editquality (edits 4/5, low) — registry.go shown in sketches but not listed as an edit. It is now named in both rationales as a file this change touches.
11. editquality (edit 6, low) — 'facts can drift between rounds; re-verify at apply time'. Re-verified at 15:40Z, AFTER another session updated the page-content-writer row at 10:16Z: container key still 'steps' (no 'substeps'), chain still generate_content -> render_section, both actions unchanged, rewrite_negations still absent, exactly one active row. The migration is anchored on all of them, so drift is 0 rows and a RAISE rather than an orphan key.

=== THE UNCHANGED CORE ===

bugs_open/305: the owner quoted two sentences built on define-by-negation and ruled this copy must never leave the framework again. The rule exists in the house voice and does not hold (migration 228's own header: 'It did not work'). The only wired detector needs a trailing ', but' and matches 23 of 1,503 sections — neither of his sentences. So: the family as one shared scanner, counted at the render and compile seams, repaired at the writer seam by replacing SENTENCES under a per-page budget, with every replacement judged for claim safety, displacement and fact preservation before it is spliced. DEMAND CONTROL, run against the three complained-of pages' real content_data with the real brief as the exemption corpus: 7 hits, 6 repairable (all headline-class, including both of the owner's sentences), 1 exempt as brief-supplied — which is the tagline, and is why this fix deliberately does not clean those pages.

plan.summary: Round 2. Add the define-by-negation family as one pure shared scanner and a content-map walker; make the existing voice gate use them; count the construction on every rendered LLM section and every compiled page (annotation only, default ON); and add a registered action that repairs the sentences beyond a per-PAGE budget of two, or any in a headline field, by splicing model-supplied replacements that must pass a claim-safety scan, a displacement check and a fact-preservation check. Enabled on one agent by a HELD migration. Plus the brief-side daily check that covers the gap the gate deliberately leaves. Round 3 carries two fixes found by round 2 (a finding-granular item_key; a truncation arm that could not fire) and routes the shared-seam scope objection to RFC_044.

edits.rationale: The family, pure and shared by every consumer so they cannot disagree about what the fault IS. Five shapes, each hit naming its containing SENTENCE with offsets into the RAW field value (a repair splices by exact substring; a sentence recovered from stripped text is not a substring of its field). ScanContrastNeighbours is a SEPARATE class that can never trip and only rejects a rewrite — without it a repair passes by moving the problem. NegationExempt is SENTENCE-scoped against brief-supplied text only, because 'rather than' is in every rendered writer prompt. AcceptNegationRewrite fails CLOSED. ROUND 2: tag comparison is now by SEQUENCE, not multiset (render_guardian: inverted nesting keeps every tag and is malformed); negative_reveal is third-person only, because the first-person form flagged 'we do not offer refunds', a policy statement the writer's own STRICT RULE 19 asks for.
edits.sketch: shapes: x_not_y | not_x_but_y | staccato | rather_than | negative_reveal neighbours (reject-only): instead_of | more_than_just | isnt_just | unlike | as_opposed_to | em_dash | … AcceptNegationRewrite(from, to, protectFrom) -> (bool, reason) empty|unchanged|gutted|ballooned|still_|displaced_|dropped_figure|invented_figure| dropped_link|markup_changed|invented_name -func sameTagMultiset(a,b) // counts equal is NOT markup preserved +func sameTagSequence(a,b) // order-equal; rejects x protectFrom = the construction's offset: facts BEFORE it are the claim and must survive; facts after it are the contrasted alternative the rewrite exists to drop.

edits.rationale: ROUND 2, and it answers bug_historian's and guardian's edit-5 objection directly: this is the traversal that was undefined at round 1. One walker for both consumers, because a repair that scanned a different set of fields from the annotation produces a count nobody can reconcile with what was fixed. It decides what counts as prose in ONE place (a cta_url or a stat value is not a sentence), returns a SORTED order because Go map order would make field paths unstable, and carries a Set closure so a repair writes through to the live map rather than into a rebuilt copy — the silent-no-op shape, designed out rather than guarded.

type NegationTextField struct { Path string; Text string; Set func(string) }
WalkContentStrings(map) []NegationTextField   // recurses maps, lists, lists-of-objects; sorted
prosey(): skips (^|_)(url|href|id|slug|class|icon|colour|value|price|email|phone|…)$, bare tokens, paths
ScanContentDataForNegation(map) []map[string]any  // field, shape, matched, sentence, headline
IsHeadlineField("items[2].heading") == true      // last segment, index-stripped
TestSetWritesThrough: mutate via the walker, assert on the ORIGINAL map (incl. items[0].description)
TestWalkerSkipsNonProse / TestWalkerOrderIsStable / TestHeadlineClassification / TestScanContentDataForNegation

edits.rationale: The existing strawman arm was blind to the shape the owner complained about; it now calls the shared scanner, so the post-deploy voice check and the meta-description gate inherit the family. ONE finding per SHAPE per block carrying that shape's count — per-hit findings would flag almost every page and tell a human nothing. 'rather than' is excluded from the per-hit path and becomes a page-level DENSITY (contrast_density, default 2, long-form 4) mirroring triad_density, because it is present in 43% of sections while the house voice permits a contrasting pair once or twice per page.

edits.rationale: The COUNT goes where it cannot be forgotten: the repair is opt-in and runs on one agent, so every other writer's fault must still be visible or the fleet figure is whatever the wired agents happen to produce. 'A gate a workflow author can forget to wire is a comment.' Annotation only — it adds result keys and changes nothing else, passes errors through untouched, and is silent on clean copy. The PAGE count re-scans each section's content_data rather than summing the per-section annotations, so a template-rendered section is still counted and a sum cannot read zero the day the metadata extractor stops forwarding a key. Wrapping at the registry rather than editing inside the two actions is deliberate: v3_site_actions.go is a 6,000-line file several sessions edit concurrently, and on 2026-08-20 it carried another session's uncommitted work referencing symbols absent at HEAD — a pathspec commit takes same-file passengers, so an inline hunk would have broken the compile at HEAD for every session. Verified by grep that nothing else in the repo calls either action directly. ROUND 3: registry.go is named here as a file this edit touches (editquality, low). And the SCOPE objection from guardian/architecture is not argued in this round — it is routed to architecture_review/RFC_044, per the 2026-07-28 ruling that a scope veto is recorded and routed rather than resubmitted with better measurements.

edits.symbol: RewriteNegationsAction (+ ActionInputSpec, + GlobalActionRegistry entry) — wired in platform/orchestration/actions/registry.go
edits.rationale: The repair, as its own registered action with its own input spec — not a key on execute_llm_prompt, which has 66 carriers and no spec (so the RFC_022 budget cannot see keys added to it) and also serves council seats and classifiers. ROUND 2 adds the two guards the council asked for: every candidate replacement goes through checkBannedClaims + loadEvidenceBase (the meta-description gate's own implementation, fleet arm ON) BEFORE the structural test, because 'say what it IS' is exactly the pressure that invents a superlative and nothing downstream inspects a spliced sentence for claim content; and a truncated repair splices NOTHING, detected both by aiservice.IsTruncated and by output_tokens reaching the max_tokens actually sent. Config resolution is ExecuteLLMPromptAction's own (resolveAIServiceConfig → createAIClient), so root/step overlay semantics are shared rather than re-invented. ROUND 3: the truncation second arm could not fire (output_tokens defaults to 0 when a provider reports no usage, so `>= max_tokens` was always false) — the three states are now distinct and UNKNOWN is logged rather than assumed safe. The splice already fails closed on a stale verbatim match; it is named in the sketch now.
edits.sketch:
scan → exempt (brief-supplied | regulatory) → page budget from CollectedData["__copy_gate"] →
ONE call for {"replacements":[{field,from,to}]} →
  negationRewriteClaimSafe(to)      // banned-claim scan FIRST (round 2)
  AcceptNegationRewrite(from,to,at) // structure, facts, displacement
  splice `to` over the verbatim `from` IN PLACE on generated_content.result
stamp __copy_gate {hits_before,hits_after,rewritten,rejected:[{field,reason}],exempt,page_hits}
one LogLLMCall row, ErrorMessage 'RETRY (bugs_open/305: define-by-negation rewrite)'
registry.go: "rewrite_negations": {Handler: RewriteNegationsAction, Category: "site", IsLocal: true}
// never returns an error for a style outcome: a page lost to a style check is worse than the tell
splice: updated := strings.Replace(text, sentence, to, 1); if updated == text -> reject 'splice_missed'
truncation: IsTruncated(err) | usageKnown := outTok > 0; only THEN compare to max_tokens; else log UNKNOWN

edits.rationale: The entire enablement surface. ROUND 2 changes: renumbered 497 → 509 (497 was taken, exactly as editquality suspected); the WHERE now anchors on the CONTAINER path ...sub_workflow,steps,... so a row keyed `substeps` matches 0 rows and RAISEs rather than inserting a step nothing runs (the round-1 gating objection, which the council's own check answered as has_steps=true — the anchor makes it enforced rather than observed); a separate _HOLD_ROLLBACK file exists, with its order load-bearing (re-point first, then delete); and the header now names TWO preconditions for un-holding it, the image AND the cross-iteration budget canary. It is _HOLD because it rewires the step CHAIN: applied before the image, every section build fails at an unknown action.

The half the gate cannot do. The gate EXEMPTS anything the site's brief supplied — a site's voice specification outranks the fleet rules — and that is precisely the route the owner's complaint arrived by: the complained-of tagline reaches the writer in 1,369 prompts and returns in 409 responses. This asks daily whether a brief HANDS the writer such a phrase, over the writer-visible surface derived at RUNTIME from the live prompt's own {{.site_specs.specs.*}} references — never data::text, which is ~4x the text the writer reads and which made an earlier fleet census wrong by 2x. Three classes kept apart: supplied (files a finding), instructional (counted only — transfer is UNMEASURED), regulatory (left alone, by calling the SAME NegationExempt the gate uses, so the two halves cannot send a human in opposite directions). LIVE and proven: 10 of 25 sites, and the close-out arm closed two sites on positive re-observation. ROUND 3, and this is the round's most important change: the item_key was per SITE while the finding is a LIST of phrases — the documented 'key coarser than its finding' trap, which drops every finding after the first while the open row goes on describing the first thing it saw. The key now carries a digest of the sorted phrase set; close-out retires an item whose phrase set no longer describes the brief, with a reason distinguishing 'now clean' from 'the phrases changed'. Proven in production: 12 site-keyed items closed and 9 refiled under phrase-set keys in one run.

visibleSurface(liveWriterConfig) -> [content_direction.formatted, identity.key_differentiators, …]

  (a site the run did not examine is never closed — an absence of evidence closes nothing)

plan.risks:
1. DISPLACEMENT ADOPTED SILENTLY — the failure that would make this worse than nothing. Mitigated by per-replacement rejection against the neighbour set, with every rejection logged WITH ITS REASON. Residual: the same instinct in a grammar nobody listed. A reviewer should read the neighbour list for a shape it misses.
2. AN OVERCLAIM SPLICED IN — round 1's compliance objection. Now gated by the estate's own banned-claims scan with the fleet arm on. Residual: an overclaim no pattern names. The prompt also forbids new capability claims explicitly, which is a rule and therefore weak on its own; the scan is the control.
3. THE PER-PAGE BUDGET'S CROSS-ITERATION STATE IS UNPROVEN AT RUNTIME. Now an explicit PRECONDITION in the held migration's header rather than a follow-up canary. Degrades to per-section (headlines still repaired) if false.
4. THE 43% ARM MAY BE TOO BROAD. 'rather than' is either a real fleet tic or too wide a pattern. It is a DENSITY in the post-deploy check for that reason, and the rejection log settles it within a week of traffic. The owning lane has been asked directly.
5. COST: ~43% of sections re-asked once at ~$0.0135 (the patch shape), ~$1.2-1.7/day at 215 sections/day; with the 119 re-ask also firing, up to three calls on one section. If anyone converts this back to a whole-section re-ask it becomes ~$200/month and materially slower builds.
6. WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: it will not clean the three pages the owner named — their tagline is brief-supplied and exempt BY DESIGN — and it holds five named FORMS rather than promising the instinct is gone. Both are stated to the owner and to the three affected lanes, in writing, before any code shipped.
7. THE SHARED-SEAM SCOPE QUESTION IS OPEN AND IS NOT THIS ROUND'S TO SETTLE: RFC_044 carries it, quoting both seats. If the architecture answer is 'declare an ActionInputSpec on both actions', that is a follow-up commit, not a change to this plan.
